AME model fitting routine for longitudinal relational data

Source: R/lame.R
lame.Rd

An MCMC routine providing a fit to an additive and multiplicative effects (AME) regression model to longitudinal (time-series) relational data of various types. Supports both unipartite (square) and bipartite (rectangular) network structures. For cross-sectional (single time point) networks, use the ame function.

Usage

lame(
  Y,
  Xdyad = NULL,
  Xrow = NULL,
  Xcol = NULL,
  rvar = TRUE,
  cvar = TRUE,
  dcor = !symmetric,
  nvar = TRUE,
  R = 0,
  R_row = NULL,
  R_col = NULL,
  mode = c("unipartite", "bipartite"),
  dynamic_uv = FALSE,
  dynamic_ab = FALSE,
  dynamic_beta = FALSE,
  dynamic_rho = FALSE,
  dynamic_beta_kind = c("ar1", "rw1", "rw2", "matern32"),
  dynamic_uv_kind = c("ar1", "snap", "t"),
  family = "normal",
  intercept = !(family == "ordinal"),
  symmetric = FALSE,
  odmax = NULL,
  prior = list(),
  g = NA,
  seed = 6886,
  nscan = 10000,
  burn = 500,
  odens = 25,
  plot = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  gof = TRUE,
  start_vals = NULL,
  periodic_save = FALSE,
  out_file = NULL,
  save_interval = 0.25,
  model.name = NULL,
  save_log_lik = FALSE,
  posterior_opts = NULL,
  log_lik_path = NULL,
  log_lik_chunk_size = 10000L,
  keep_snap_draws = c("none", "summary", "draws"),
  freeze_call = FALSE,
  dynamic_beta_pool = c("none", "rho", "sigma", "both"),
  dynamic_beta_per_actor = NULL,
  per_actor_covariate_idx = 1L,
  per_actor_identifiability = c("center", "exact_center"),
  keep_per_actor = c("auto", "draws", "summary", "none"),
  time_index = NULL,
  period_exposure = NULL,
  max_seconds = Inf,
  checkpoint_path = NULL,
  checkpoint_every = 100L,
  log_lik_method = c("observed_exact", "observed_ghk", "augmented"),
  ordinal_cutpoints = c("data_induced", "explicit"),
  method = c("mcmc", "als"),
  als_stability = c("none", "quick", "validation"),
  als_max_iter = 1000L,
  als_tol = NULL,
  als_lowrank_method = NULL,
  als_linear_solver = NULL,
  als_multistart = NULL,
  multistart = c("none", "cheap", "full"),
  bootstrap = 0L,
  bootstrap_type = c("parametric", "block"),
  bootstrap_block_length = 1L,
  bootstrap_seed = NULL,
  chains = .lame_chains_default(),
  cores = NULL,
  resume_from = NULL,
  sampler = c("gibbs", "tempered")
)

Arguments

Y

a T length list of relational matrices, or a 3D array of dimensions [n_row, n_col, T], where T is the number of time periods. Named lists may have changing actor composition; actors are aligned by row and column names. A longitudinal netify object is also accepted and converted with netify::to_lame(lame = TRUE). When family or mode is omitted, the value inferred by netify is used. See family below for data types.

Xdyad

a T length list of n x n x pd arrays of covariates

Xrow

a T length list of n x pr matrices of nodal row covariates. In a symmetric model (symmetric = TRUE) each node covariate enters a dyad through both of its actors.

Xcol

a T length list of n x pc matrices of nodal column covariates. In a symmetric model a node covariate may be given in Xrow, in Xcol or in both, and each distinct covariate enters once, as <name>_node.

rvar

logical: fit row random effects (asymmetric case)? With method = "als" and a normal, binary or Poisson dynamic fit by the empirical-Bayes estimator, rvar, cvar, nvar and dcor are honoured (a disabled margin is a point mass at zero, as in the sampler; see dcor for the correlation); the penalised routes name them in the warning about ignored arguments.

cvar

logical: fit column random effects (asymmetric case)? See rvar for method = "als".

dcor

logical: fit a dyadic correlation (asymmetric case)? The correlation \(\rho\) of the two residuals of a dyad carries the prior \(p(\rho) \propto 1 - \rho^2\) on \((-1, 1)\), which vanishes at the boundaries. Information about it depends on joint presence and absence of ties and the fitted means. With fewer than one mutual dyad per period, or fewer than 30 in all, the data inform it mainly through the absence of mutual ties, and a message gives the count. Its posterior can then stay near the prior or move well away from it: toward -1 when the fitted means predict more mutual ties than the panel has (on the 40-state MID panel, -0.58 with 95 percent interval -0.92 to -0.13). The additive effects, coefficients and latent positions all retain the same sampled correlation, including on panels with few mutual dyads. dynamic_uv = TRUE keeps the correlation: the per-period position kernel whitens each dyad's pair of residuals by the current \(\rho\), exactly as the static-position kernel does, so the reciprocity is carried by \(\rho\) instead of being absorbed into the coordinates. A period-varying \(\rho\) (dynamic_rho) needs static positions. A Poisson residual variance below 0.1 leaves \(\rho\) to its prior in the same way, and a message says so. An exactly symmetric Y fitted with symmetric = FALSE has equal reciprocal residuals, so the posterior of \(\rho\) concentrates near one (with dcor = FALSE the two cells of a dyad count as two observations); a message says so and points at symmetric = TRUE, which fits the undirected model. A normal model with dcor = TRUE has no proper posterior once the reciprocal pairs of the panel outnumber what its mean parameters absorb by four (the bound ame applies, pooled over the periods: they share \(\rho\), so the excess of every period adds, and a parameter they share absorbs its contrasts once): \(\rho\) runs to one, with static or dynamic positions or none, and the variance draw breaks down. Such a fit is an error of class lame_symmetric_y. With method = "als" a directed binary fit (the probit link of the empirical-Bayes default) models the correlation: the two cells of a dyad are one bivariate probit observation, the correlation is one number for all periods (fit$VC["rho"]; the record, with its standard deviation, in fit$rho_estimation and fit$eb$pair), and it is estimated with the other hyperparameters under the prior above. A directed Poisson fit takes the two counts of a dyad as one observation at the fitted state of independent cells: the correlation is the posterior mean, under the same prior, of the profile of the pair probability, and the information of the pairs enters the standard errors. A directed normal fit takes the two cells of a dyad as one bivariate normal observation, in closed form, and estimates the correlation under the same prior; a directed network whose reciprocal pairs are all exactly equal is an error of class "lame_improper_normal_reciprocity", as in ame (fit it with symmetric = TRUE or dcor = FALSE). dcor = FALSE fits independent cells. Undirected and bipartite networks have no pair of cells. On the dynamic route the pair of cells of a binary fit is integrated over the uncertainty of its latent factors or moving positions, and the fit takes 1.4 to 2.7 times as long as the independent-cell fit (1.4 with additive effects only, 1.9 to 2.7 with static factors or moving positions); options(lame.als_threads) splits the work over threads and changes nothing else.

nvar

logical: fit nodal random effects (symmetric case)? See rvar for method = "als".

R

integer: dimension of the multiplicative effects (can be zero). A binary fit whose multiplicative term reproduces the observed ties exactly is separated: the size of the term is then set by its prior, the fit says so, and the signs and the fitted probabilities are what the data determine; a smaller R (down to zero for a panel whose ties barely change over time) reproduces them without saturating. With method = "als" and dynamic_uv = FALSE, the latent factors of a normal, binary or Poisson dynamic fit are static and have the variational posterior of the static estimator (ame_als): their posterior means are reported as U and V, the scale of their prior in fit$eb$factor_prior, and the standard errors are marginal over the factors and carry the uncertainty of that scale (fit$eb$factor_scale$sd_log; options(lame.eb_scale_uncertainty = FALSE) leaves it out).

R_row

integer: for bipartite networks, dimension of row node multiplicative effects (defaults to R)

R_col

integer: for bipartite networks, dimension of column node multiplicative effects (defaults to R)

mode

character: either "unipartite" (default) for square networks or "bipartite" for rectangular networks

dynamic_uv

logical: fit dynamic multiplicative effects (latent factors). The transition model is selected by dynamic_uv_kind. A directed fit with dynamic positions carries the dyadic correlation of dcor through the position kernel (see dcor). fit$U / fit$V hold the positions factored from each period's posterior mean product (see latent_positions); the per-iteration cubes are kept as fit$U_draws / fit$V_draws by the default posterior_opts (or with posterior_opts = list(save_UV_draws = TRUE)), and give the posterior standard deviations. Default FALSE. With method = "als" and a normal, binary or Poisson outcome the positions are estimated by the dynamic empirical-Bayes estimator: fit$U and fit$V are the posterior means (n x R x T) with posterior standard deviations fit$U_sd and fit$V_sd, fit$Oarr (alias fit$UVPM) is the posterior-mean product, fit$rho_uv and fit$sigma_uv are the persistence and innovation scale of the positions, smoothing settings chosen by the fit rather than estimates (prediction, simulation and warm starts read them; the sampler estimates the persistence with an interval), and fit$eb$uv_scale and fit$eb$uv_search are the stationary variance and the search that chose it. Directed, bipartite (R_row and R_col may differ: the interaction has rank min(R_row, R_col)) and undirected networks are covered.

dynamic_ab

logical: fit dynamic additive effects (sender/receiver effects) that evolve over time. When TRUE, the row effects (a) and column effects (b) become time-varying as a per-actor level plus an AR(1) deviation (see the model description in the details). This captures temporal heterogeneity in actors' baseline propensities to send and receive ties, allowing for smooth changes in activity levels and popularity over time. For example, an actor's tendency to form outgoing ties might gradually increase or decrease across observation periods. The AR(1) specification ensures temporal smoothness while allowing for actor-specific evolution patterns. Implementation uses conjugate updates where possible and C++ for computational efficiency. Default FALSE. Each dynamic effect is a per-actor level plus a zero-mean AR(1) deviation: the level is pooled over every period (its variance is the reported va / vb) and the deviation carries the persistence rho_ab and innovation scale sigma_ab. The marginal variance of a per-period effect is therefore va + sigma_ab^2 / (1 - rho_ab^2), and rho_ab describes the deviations, so on short panels it reads lower than the persistence of the raw effect path. Both parts are drawn from the likelihood: the levels given the deviations and the deviations given the levels, so persistent actor heterogeneity lives in the effects. The regression coefficients are drawn conditional on the current effects, and the effects are drawn conditional on summing to zero in every period when an intercept is included. Under that constraint an individual actor's marginal variance has the additional factor 1 - 1/n, where n is the number of actors in that margin.

Because the effects of every period sum to zero, a static intercept would leave no room for a shift common to all actors in one period (the whole network busier in period t), which the data identify. With an intercept the intercept is therefore a dynamic_beta coefficient whenever dynamic_ab = TRUE: it is added to the coefficients that dynamic_beta names, and dynamic_beta = FALSE gives a dynamic intercept alone (its own block). The added intercept is a random walk ("rw1") when dynamic_beta_kind is "ar1", so its forecasts hold the last level of the network. Blocks the user names keep dynamic_beta_kind; with "rw1", "rw2" or "matern32" the intercept takes that kind. fit$dynamic_beta_kind_by_block gives the kind of each block, and an "rw1" block holds RHO_BETA = 1. BETA is then an iterations x coefficients x periods array, and fit$dynamic_intercept_from_ab records that the rule added the intercept. The rule applies with dynamic_rho = TRUE, whose coefficient paths are filtered under each period's \(\rho_t\), and with the tempered sampler, which carries the random-walk intercept in its replica state.

The reported intercept and effects are the identified quantities when the fit has a multiplicative term; see the details.

A directed binary panel carrying fewer than 1.2 events per actor-period (two periods or more) reports va and vb as not estimated, and fewer than 0.6 (1.6 with a multiplicative term) its intercept. On simulated panels of 30 actors and 5 periods (static and dynamic effects, ranks 0 and 1, 64 to 252 panels a rate bin) the 95 percent intervals of va and vb covered 0.31 and 0.28 of the panels below 0.6 events per actor-period, 0.73 and 0.68 from 0.6 to 0.9, 0.91 and 0.81 from 0.9 to 1.2, and 0.91 to 1.00 from 1.2; the intercept covered 0.57 to 0.87 of the panels below its rate and 0.92 or more from it. The persistence rho_ab (coverage 1.00 at every rate) and the innovation scale sigma_ab (0.84 to 1.00) are reported at every rate, and so is cab (0.97 to 1.00). The draws remain in fit$VC and fit$BETA; fit$events_per_actor_period and fit$events_per_actor record the event rates. Supplying an effects prior (prior$Sab0, eta0 or etaab) reports va and vb under that explicit prior, which the summary names. Count families keep reporting their variance components. The stored paths a_dynamic and b_dynamic contain the full level-plus-deviation effects. Static latent positions are centered for reporting, with the removed product components carried by the reported intercept and effects. Dynamic latent coordinates retain the coordinates drawn under their proper path prior. Compare fitted predictors and per-period products across chains; raw coordinates can differ through latent rotations.

dynamic_beta

logical, character, integer, or logical-vector flag selecting which regression coefficients evolve over time via independent AR(1) processes. Default FALSE keeps every coefficient static (the historical behaviour). Accepted forms:

  • FALSE / NULL: no coefficient is dynamic.

  • TRUE: every coefficient is dynamic.

  • character vector of block shortcuts ("intercept", "dyad", "row", "col") or specific coefficient names from colnames(BETA) – those become dynamic.

  • integer vector: 1-based column indices into colnames(BETA).

  • logical vector of length p: per-coefficient mask.

Each dynamic-coefficient block (one per distinct intercept / dyad / row / col label that has at least one dynamic coefficient) gets its own AR(1) parameters \(\rho_\beta\) (truncated-Normal prior, default mean 0.8, bounded between 0 and 0.999) and \(\sigma_\beta^2\) (inverse-Gamma prior, default shape 2 with a scale set from the response scale, see prior). The joint posterior over the time path \(\beta_t\) is drawn by Forward-Filter / Backward-Sample (FFBS) inside the MCMC loop, conditional on the current static-block beta and on (a, b, U, V). When the intercept or a nodal coefficient is dynamic, a sum-to-zero contrast basis is applied to the additive-effect sampler to keep \(a_i + intercept_t\) identified. Requires at least 2 time periods. dynamic_beta composes with multiplicative latent factors (R > 0) and additive random effects for every family, across unipartite/bipartite and directed/symmetric panels and in combination with dynamic_ab / dynamic_uv. An AR(1) coefficient reverts to its own long-run mean \(\mu_k\): $$\beta_{k,t} - \mu_k = \rho_\beta (\beta_{k,t-1} - \mu_k) + e_{k,t}, \quad e_{k,t} \sim N(0, \sigma_\beta^2 \lambda_k),$$ with the first period drawn from the stationary law \(N(\mu_k, \sigma_\beta^2 \lambda_k / (1 - \rho_\beta^2))\), where \(\lambda_k\) is the innovation scale of the coefficient (one over the mean square of its covariate). \(\mu_k\) has the prior the coefficient has when static (see g): in a unipartite fit the marginal of the panel prior on its column, with precision from sum_t(crossprod(X_t)) / (T g) and free of \(s^2\); in a bipartite fit \(N(0, g_k s^2)\) with \(g_k\) the default g over the mean square of the covariate column (g itself for the intercept or a user-supplied g) and \(s^2\) the dyadic variance (one for the probit and rank families). It is drawn from its Gaussian conditional given the path and \((\rho_\beta, \sigma_\beta)\); the path is drawn given \(\mu_k\). \(\rho_\beta\) is therefore the persistence of the coefficient's movement around its level, and an \(h\)-step forecast of the coefficient reverts to \(\mu_k\) as \(\rho_\beta^h\). The long-run means are fit$mu_beta (posterior means) and fit$MU_BETA (draws, one column per AR(1) coefficient); print(), summary(), confint(fit, parm = "mu_beta") and trace_plot() report them and the convergence checks monitor them. Random-walk ("rw1"), "rw2" and "matern32" paths have no long-run mean. An "rw2" or "matern32" path is its first-period level, with the prior of a static coefficient, plus its change since then: under "rw2" the first increment is \(N(0, \sigma_\beta^2 \lambda_k)\) and so is each second difference; under "matern32" the change is that of a Matern 3/2 process with variance \(\sigma_\beta^2 \lambda_k\) and length scale prior$matern32_length_scale (default \(\max(2, T/4)\)). The tempered sampler carries the same laws, and an \(h\)-step forecast draws the future periods from their conditional given the fitted ones. With a single dynamic coefficient block and small \(T\), only \(T - 1\) transitions inform its AR(1) persistence, so the data inform \(\rho_\beta\) weakly and its posterior stays near the prior; the path BETA[, k, ] is read separately from the hyperparameters, and dynamic_beta_prior_summary shows the paths the prior implies. The hyperparameters of each block (\(\rho_\beta\) and \(\sigma_\beta\), and the pooled scale and persistence of dynamic_beta_pool) are drawn from their exact conditionals given the path at every sweep (a draw costs well under a millisecond). Earlier versions drew them every 20th sweep; on normal and binary panels that left the scale and the persistence with 4 to 20 times fewer effective draws (panels of 5 to 170 actors; at 170 actors 357 of 1,600 draws of the scale on a normal panel and 304 on a binary one, where every sweep gives 1,599 and 1,335). An interweaving step also moves the hyperparameters together with the path, before the path is redrawn given them. It proposes new values of \((\sigma_\beta, \rho_\beta)\) by a symmetric walk on \((\log \sigma_\beta, \mathrm{logit}\,\rho_\beta)\), rebuilds the path from the same standardised innovations (the state equation divided by the innovation scale; "rw2" and "matern32": the first period stays fixed and the change since then scales with \(\sigma_\beta\), the length scale being fixed) and accepts with the Metropolis ratio of the likelihood of the rebuilt path and the hyperprior (the pooled hierarchies included). It targets the funnel of hierarchical models: where the data say little about the path (few actors, many periods) and the prior of the scale is diffuse, the centred draws alone move the scale slowly, because the scale given the path is pinned at the spread of the path in hand. On a panel of six actors and 30 periods with prior$sigma_beta_shape = 0.5 and prior$sigma_beta_scale = 1e-4 the step raised the effective draws of the scale 2.8 times and those of the persistence 2.0 times over the draws at every sweep; at the default prior it raised them 1.0 to 1.5 times on the panels checked (5 to 30 actors, 12 to 60 periods), which about repays the time it takes there (10 to 60 percent of a sweep). Where the data pin the path (a dense panel) about nine proposals in ten are rejected and the step costs 3 percent of a sweep at 170 actors. prior$beta_hyper_nc = FALSE omits the step, and fit$beta_hyper_move records its attempts and accepts. With method = "als", selected intercept, dyadic, row-node, and column-node coefficients are supported on normal, binary, and Poisson panels, including named panels where actors enter or exit. Dynamic ALS uses period-specific Xrow or Xcol values for selected dynamic node coefficients; static node coefficients still use per-actor means. The ALS estimator fits the same long-run means (fit$mu_beta), as random effects under the static coefficient prior, with Laplace standard errors in fit$eb$mu_beta_se. Dynamic intercepts are unavailable when family = "ordinal". Default FALSE.

dynamic_rho

logical. For directed unipartite normal models, allow the residual dyadic reciprocity parameter \(\rho_t\) to vary by period instead of using one pooled dyadic correlation across the whole panel. It requires static latent positions (dynamic_uv = FALSE) and combines with dynamic_beta, whose paths are filtered under each period's \(\rho_t\). MCMC fits store per-draw paths in fit$RHO and the posterior mean path in fit$rho_path. This option is not supported with method = "als"; use a supported MCMC configuration for period-specific reciprocity. Dynamic ALS fits use one pooled correlation, fit$VC["rho"], and report period-specific residual diagnostics in fit$residual_rho_path. The legacy fit$rho_path field remains a diagnostic alias, labelled by fit$rho_path_role = "residual_diagnostic"; it is not a fitted covariance path. als_start_vals() uses the pooled ALS correlation, including for legacy ALS objects. Default FALSE.

dynamic_beta_kind

character: state-space prior on the dynamic coefficient block(s). "ar1" (default) gives mean-reverting AR(1) with a truncated-Normal prior on \(\rho_\beta\). "rw1" gives a random walk (\(\rho_\beta\) pinned at 1, no truncation), appropriate when you expect permanent drift with no mean reversion – e.g. trade-gravity coefficients in a permanently changing world economy. The alias "random_walk" is also accepted for "rw1". When the stationarity warning in summary(fit) fires under the default AR(1), refit with dynamic_beta_kind = "rw1" for cleaner inference. Decision tree: mean-reverting? AR(1). Permanent / unit-root drift? RW1. Smooth with curvature? "rw2" (second-order random walk). Smooth with a known length-scale? "matern32" (Matern 3/2). Note: "rw2" and "matern32" use an R-level joint Gaussian sampler and run substantially slower per iteration than the C++ FFBS used for "ar1" / "rw1" (roughly 2-4x on n = 100, T = 10). On method = "als" the coefficient paths are "ar1", "rw1" or "rw2", including the empirical-Bayes estimator; "matern32" is refused there and needs method = "mcmc".

dynamic_uv_kind

Character string selecting the transition model for dynamic multiplicative latent positions when dynamic_uv = TRUE. "ar1" uses Gaussian AR(1) drift, "snap" uses a mixture of AR(1) drift and discontinuous reset transitions, and "t" uses heavy-tailed Student-t innovations represented by local transition scales, with (in the MCMC sampler) a Student-t first period of the same degrees of freedom and the stationary scale (see Details). On the MCMC path, "snap" is available for directed, bipartite and symmetric fits and "t" for directed unipartite fits, at any rank (the symmetric product's unit-variance coordinates do not hold their scale under the scale-mixture transitions). A bipartite snap fit carries the resets of its row and of its column actors, each with its own paths, under one persistence, innovation scale and reset rate; a symmetric one carries one set of unit-variance paths, so its linked reset scale is 1. Under "snap", a reset lands on the stationary distribution of the position paths unless prior$snap_kappa fixes its scale, and rho_uv and sigma_uv are updated jointly with the latent reset indicators. Each actor's whole path is also drawn with its resets summed out (prior$actor_move_paths, see Details), so a period change can pass between a reset and a drift explanation. At every rank, summary(), print() and trace_plot() report rho_uv, sigma_uv and the reset rate pi_snap of a "snap" fit, and the two-chain check monitors them; at rank two or more the exact rotation move (prior$uv_rotation_move) keeps the orientations of the periods of a directed fit aligned, and bipartite and symmetric fits draw their own gauge given the resets. They report rho_uv and sigma_uv of a "t" fit at every rank too, and the check monitors them. A "t" chain starts from a dynamic ALS fit by default (prior$als_start); that is a warm start only, and a chain started cold reports and monitors them the same way. Both kinds receive conditional sign updates that preserve the fitted products and help chains explore alternative trajectory orientations. With method = "als", "snap" is refused. The ALS "t" kind supports directed and symmetric normal, binary and Poisson panels; bipartite Student ALS is refused. A normal, binary or Poisson fit is fitted by the dynamic empirical-Bayes estimator for "ar1" (Gaussian) and "t" transitions (directed and undirected networks): the weights of the scale mixture have a variational posterior, and the degrees of freedom are prior$t_nu (default 4). ALS Student-t dynamic UV fits attach the final local transition-weight matrices as fit$lambda_u and fit$lambda_v (n x T, one in the first period).

family

character: one of "normal","binary","ordinal","cbin","frn","poisson" - see the details below

intercept

logical: fit model with an intercept?

symmetric

logical: is the sociomatrix symmetric? Not available for the "cbin" and "frn" families, whose per-actor ranked nominations are directed by construction. A symmetric fit needs a symmetric Y in every period and symmetric Xdyad slices, as in ame: the regression term of a symmetric fit is symmetric, so an asymmetric slice is an error (class lame_symmetric_xdyad) that names the slice and the first period; so is it with method = "als". Replace it by (X + t(X)) / 2. A value missing in one triangle of a slice is not an asymmetry: it is filled from the other triangle.

odmax

a scalar integer or vector of length n giving the maximum number of nominations that each node may make - used for "frn" and "cbin" families. A cap below a row's observed out-degree contradicts Y and is an error. A cap that most rows' observed outdegrees reach erases the cross-row spread in outdegree that the sender effects rest on: a row at its cap shows only that its level is high enough to fill the cap. The sampler pools the prior scale of the row side with the column side once 80 percent of the observed rows (60 percent in a single period) nominate the full odmax, counting a row with hidden cells by what a full cap thins to at its observed share; fit$odmax_saturated_share records the share and fit$odmax_sat_threshold the threshold. va, vb and cab are reported at every share: on simulated panels of 24 to 30 actors their 95 percent intervals covered the generating values in 0.88 to 1.00 of the panels at every share, with and without a fifth of the cells hidden and at generating sender sds of 0.25, 0.5 and 1 (at 0.25 the posterior mean of va runs up to 2.3 times the generating variance while the interval still covers). va and the level of the rows follow the design. A design of two periods or more with a cap share of 0.5 or more and a posterior-mean va from 0.5 to 1.5 reports the intercept and the row-covariate coefficients as not estimated: the rows below the cap carry too little of the spread of the senders and the posterior of va sits near its prior. In simulated panels (24 actors, 4 and 6 periods, one chain at the package defaults, 1440 fits at generating sender sds of 0.5, 1 and 1.5) the intercept was covered in 0.89 of the 312 panels in that region (0.76 at sd 0.5 and 1.5, 0.97 at sd 1) and in 0.96 of the 1128 outside it. va is reported in the region: its interval covered 0.91 of the 312 panels (0.79 at sd 0.5, 1.00 at sd 1, 0.72 at sd 1.5) and 0.99 outside it. The posterior mean of va ran 0.18 and 0.23 above the generating variance at sd 0.5 (shares 0.3 and 0.7), 0.08 and 0.00 above it at sd 1 and 0.02 and 0.18 below it at sd 1.5. In a single period (ame() and one-period lame() fits) a row at its cap leaves the level of the rows unbounded above: with every row at the cap the intercept interval covered 0.64 of the panels, and with cells hidden and a share from 0.5 it covered 0.84, against 0.98 or more elsewhere. The intercept and any row-covariate coefficient are reported as not estimated there, with the draws kept in fit$BETA. On 200 simulated 170 by 100 bipartite panels (cap 10, shares 0.3 and 0.7) the intercept was covered in 1.00 of the panels, vb in 0.98 to 1.00 and va in 0.90 to 1.00, its posterior mean 0.09 to 0.15 below the generating variance; nothing is withheld there. When the effects prior is supplied (prior$Sab0, eta0 or etaab), the fit names the prior in the summary (fit$prior_supplied records it); a prior on the effects does not fix the level of a row, so the intercept stays withheld in those designs, and va is reported under that prior. A cap the design itself imposes cannot be relaxed: read APM / BPM as relative sender and receiver levels there.

prior

a list containing hyperparameters for the prior distributions. Available options and their defaults:

s20

Fixed positive prior scale for the dyadic residual variance \(v_e\). The prior has one degree of freedom. By default, normal fits use the variance of the observed responses, computed once before sampling; constant responses use their mean square, or 1 if all zero. Poisson fits use 1 on the latent log-rate scale. The resolved scale is reported as fit$s2_prior_scale. It is never recomputed from the current residuals. A supplied value overrides this default. The coefficient prior is controlled separately by g.

uv_prior

For sampler = "tempered", "hierarchical" (default) or the explicitly different "unit" coordinate prior. This option is refused on the Gibbs route. See Details.

Sab0

Prior scale matrix for the additive-effects covariance. A 2x2 matrix where Sab0\[1,1\] is the prior variance for row effects, Sab0\[2,2\] is the prior variance for column effects, and off-diagonals control correlation between row and column effects. For the "normal" and "poisson" families, and for unipartite "binary", "ordinal", "cbin" and "frn", this defaults to diag(2) scaled to the observed sender/receiver heterogeneity in Y (for the ordinal, cbin and frn families, of its probit-moment scores) rather than to a fixed diag(2); see ame for the rationale. For "cbin" and "frn" panels of at least two periods the two sides get their own scale, the row side read with the rows at their nomination cap as censored observations. This keeps the receiver spread from setting the sender's prior scale when capped outdegrees contain little sender information. Where the rows at the cap reach the reporting threshold of odmax the pooled scale is kept. Bipartite fits of the probit-scale families use diag(2). Pass diag(2) explicitly for a fixed unit-scale prior.

eta0

Prior degrees of freedom for the additive-effects covariance \(\Sigma_{ab}\) (default: round(4 \* vdfmlt) for unipartite "binary", "ordinal", "cbin" and "frn" fits, where vdfmlt is a probit-moment variance multiplier estimated from Y, and round(4 + 3 \* n/100) otherwise, where n is the number of actors; 1 for a "poisson" fit, whose default Sab0 is the effects covariance the fast route (lame_als) estimates for the same panel, or the log-rate scale where that fit fails; see ame). Higher values impose stronger shrinkage of the row/column effects toward the prior scale. The multiplicative-effects static unipartite prior is the one of ame: an inverse-Wishart covariance with the degrees of freedom and the data-scaled Suv0 of kappa0 and Suv0 in ame, read off every period of the panel (the static factors are shared by the periods). Suv0 and kappa0 apply to ame of a unipartite network only; a bipartite network has no such covariance, and supplying either is an error of class "lame_prior_unused".

etaab

Prior degrees of freedom for covariance of additive effects (default: 4 + 3 \* n/100). Controls shrinkage of row/column random effects.

ab_min_observed

Observation count used to shrink sparse actor initial values (default: max(10, T)). Subsequent actor updates use the specified Gaussian prior without deterministic shrinkage.

rho_uv_mean

For dynamic_uv=TRUE: Prior mean of the persistence \(\rho_{uv}\) of the latent positions, a normal prior truncated to (-0.99, 0.99). Default 0.7 on the MCMC path for every family, kind and mode (the dynamic ALS estimator keeps 0.5 for Gaussian bipartite AR(1) fits and 0.9 otherwise). Values close to 1 indicate high persistence.

rho_uv_sd

For dynamic_uv=TRUE: Prior SD of \(\rho_{uv}\). Default 0.3 on the MCMC path (the ALS estimator keeps 0.2 and 0.1). A setting of either is used as given and the other keeps its default, so a fit that sets both is unchanged by the default. The data see \(|\rho_{uv}|\) only (see uv_rho_flip_move) and the draws are stored with \(\rho_{uv} \ge 0\), so the prior acts through its mass folded onto [0, 0.99). The default comes from a simulation study (AR(1) positions at rank two, 20 and 40 actors, 4, 6 and 10 periods, true persistence 0.3, 0.6 and 0.9, normal, binary and Poisson responses, the three kinds and the three modes; 522 panels, the posterior under each candidate prior reweighted from one fit under a nearly flat prior). Under the former default N(0.9, 0.1) the 90 percent intervals covered a true 0.3, 0.6 and 0.9 in 11, 51 and 82 percent of the panels (mean standardised bias +5.3, +1.6 and -0.2 posterior sd); under N(0.7, 0.3) they cover in 90, 88 and 80 percent (+0.36, +0.22 and -0.22). Flatter priors (N(0.5, 0.5), a uniform, a Beta(9, 2) on \((\rho + 1)/2\)) did no better and priors whose sd shrinks with the Fisher information of the panel did worse; the former Gaussian bipartite N(0.5, 0.2) pulled a persistence of 0.9 down without helping at 0.3. The low coverage of a true 0.9 in binary and Poisson panels that this study left came from the prior on the innovation variance (see uv_var_shape). Under the "t" kind, whose first period has the tail of its transitions, directed panels of Gaussian AR(1) paths (20 actors, 6 periods, 24 panels per family and persistence) are covered in 85, 86 and 86 percent at a true 0.3, 0.6 and 0.9 (mean standardised bias +0.50, -0.18 and +0.13); with a Gaussian first period and the inverse gamma on \(\sigma_{uv}^2\) they were covered in 79, 92 and 68 percent (+0.68, +0.18 and +0.20). Directed Poisson panels at a true 0.3 are the low cell: on the 24 panels of that study (20 actors, 6 periods) the "t" kind covers 67 percent (+1.24) and "ar1" 75 percent (+0.92). The panels' own paths place the persistence +0.25 sd above the average panel and the prior adds +0.4 sd (a nearly flat prior gives +0.85), and the heavy-tailed transitions read the estimation noise of weakly identified count positions as innovations: \(\rho_{uv}\) sits 0.031 higher than under "ar1" on the same panels (0.002 with prior$t_nu = 50, 0.045 over 12 periods, where the "t" kind covers 75 percent at +1.10 against "ar1"'s 75 percent at +0.31, and 0.010 with 40 actors, where it covers 83 percent at +0.33). On Poisson panels whose paths have Student-t transitions, the kind's own model, it covers a true 0.3 in 92 percent of 24 panels at 6 periods (+0.14) and in all 12 at 12 periods (-0.11).

uv_var_shape

For dynamic_uv=TRUE: shape of the inverse-gamma prior on the stationary variance \(w = \sigma_{uv}^2 / (1 - \rho_{uv}^2)\) of a latent coordinate path, independent of \(\rho_{uv}\) (default 2). Given \(\rho_{uv}\) it is the inverse gamma with scale uv_var_scale \(\times (1 - \rho_{uv}^2)\) on the innovation variance, so the innovations shrink with the persistence. It is the default unless sigma_uv_shape or sigma_uv_scale is set; setting both kinds is an error. The default comes from a simulation study (AR(1) positions at rank two, directed and bipartite, normal, binary and Poisson, 20 actors over 4 and 10 periods and 40 actors over 4, true persistence 0.3, 0.6 and 0.9, and the "t" and "snap" kinds on directed binary and Poisson panels; 336 panels, every candidate reweighted from one fit under a nearly flat prior). The former default, an inverse gamma IG(2, b) on \(\sigma_{uv}^2\), pulls a persistent path toward a lower \(\rho_{uv}\): given the stationary variance, which the data fix, its density in \(\rho_{uv}\) falls as \(\exp(-b / (w (1 - \rho_{uv}^2)))\). Its 90 percent intervals covered a true 0.9 in 76 percent of the panels (mean standardised bias -0.84 posterior sd; 62 percent and -1.7 for directed Poisson panels, 75 percent and -0.9 for binary ones), and removing or halving uv_var_cap changed nothing, since the stationary variance never came near it. Under the default the intervals cover a true 0.3, 0.6 and 0.9 in 96, 90 and 86 percent of the panels (+0.23, +0.16 and -0.18), directed binary 0.9 in 92 percent and directed Poisson 0.9 in 85 percent of the AR(1) and snap panels (+0.16). Inverse gammas of shape 1, 1.5 and 3, scales from 0.1 b to 2 b, half-t and flat priors on \(w\) did as well within Monte Carlo error, and a scale of b / 2 gave the best coverage of directed Poisson panels; inverse gammas on \(\sigma_{uv}^2\) with smaller scales or a half-Cauchy on \(\sigma_{uv}\) moved the persistence at 0.3 and 0.6 up by about 0.1 posterior sd. With this prior the posterior allows the small innovation variances of persistent paths, which the conditional draws of the paths and of \((\rho_{uv}, w)\) cross slowly, so directed and bipartite fits of the "ar1" kind also take a non-centred update of \((\rho_{uv}, w)\) with the whitened innovations held fixed, binary and Poisson fits also with the latent array carried along the product (fit$uv_nc_hyper_move). On the release sweep's dynamic positions cells the two-chain check then extends the chains as often as under the former prior (1.22 against 1.23 extensions a fit over 144 fits, none refused).

uv_var_scale

For dynamic_uv=TRUE: scale of that prior. Default b / 2, where b is 1 and, for the normal family of a directed unipartite network, the typical size of the additive effects (the scale of the factor prior above), so the prior is the same for a response measured in other units; the positions of a bipartite or undirected network are unit free, the interaction matrix and the weights carrying the unit. Symmetric fits draw neither variance: their coordinate paths have unit stationary variance, so the innovation SD is \(\sqrt{1 - \rho_{uv}^2}\) and the diagonal L of the product carries the scale.

sigma_uv_shape

For dynamic_uv=TRUE: shape of an inverse-gamma prior on the innovation variance \(\sigma_{uv}^2\) itself, used instead of the stationary-variance prior when this or sigma_uv_scale is set (the other then defaults to 2 for the shape and to b for the scale). Fits and checkpoints written with these settings, including those of lame 1.4.1 and earlier, whose default this was, are unchanged.

sigma_uv_scale

For dynamic_uv=TRUE: scale of that inverse-gamma prior on \(\sigma_{uv}^2\).

uv_max_abs

For dynamic_uv=TRUE: absolute bound on each free latent coordinate. Each actor-vector conditional rejects proposals outside this joint prior support. Default 8 for binary, ordinal, cbin and frn families and 50 for normal and Poisson families (the bound of a unipartite normal fit is multiplied by the square root of sd(Y): its coordinates carry the square root of the unit of the response). Set to Inf to remove the restriction. A finite bound changes the prior; no deterministic coordinate normalization is applied. The box is part of the prior on the scale of the positions, which the data do not fix in a bipartite fit (the interaction matrix carries it) and which uv_var_cap already limits: on the validation panels (50 actors, 5 periods; bipartite 40 by 30) the largest coordinate drawn under the default box was 7.8 (the box is 8 on the probit scale) and 6.9 with the box removed, a proposal fell outside it in at most 1 of 10000 sweeps, and the coefficients, variance components, fitted values and posterior mean of the product \(U G V'\) with and without the box differed by about as much as two chains of the same fit do (at most 0.0014 root-mean-square for the product, and none for the cbin and Poisson panels, where no proposal came near the box). It matters when a fit separates the data: without it the product runs away.

G_max

For bipartite fits with a static interaction matrix: absolute bound on entries of \(G\). A joint Gaussian conditional proposal outside the bound is rejected. Default 20 for binary, ordinal, cbin and frn families with dynamic_uv=TRUE and 100 otherwise (multiplied by sd(Y) for the normal family: the interaction matrix carries the unit of the response). Set to Inf to remove this prior restriction. On the validation panels the largest entry drawn was 2.7, a tenth of the default bound, and no proposal fell outside it.

sigma_uv_max

For dynamic_uv=TRUE: rail on the innovation SD of the latent coordinate paths. Default 10 for bipartite fits, where \(G\) absorbs the scale, and none for unipartite fits. On the validation panels the posterior of the innovation SD stayed below 1.4, a seventh of the rail.

uv_var_cap

For dynamic_uv=TRUE: bound on the stationary variance of a latent coordinate path. This is joint prior support for sigma_uv and rho_uv; both updates respect it. A finite cap also constrains the residual-variance update for normal responses. The bound is a multiple of the observation variance for the normal family and absolute on the latent scale otherwise: the binary, ordinal, cbin and frn families fix that variance at one, and for the Poisson family the latent scale is the log rate, whose overdispersion variance does not enter. Default 4 for the binary, Poisson, ordinal, cbin and frn families and Inf for the normal family. In a bipartite fit the interaction matrix carries the scale of the paths and the data do not identify it, so the posterior of the stationary variance lies against this bound (within 10 percent of the default in 29 percent of the sweeps of the validation panel, against none in the unipartite ones; without the bound its 1st to 99th percentiles run from 3 to 76). Between a cap of 4, a cap of 16 and none the coefficients and the variance components of the validation fit moved by at most 1.2 percent, while rho_uv, sigma_uv and the norms of U and V follow the cap: read a bipartite fit through the product \(U G V'\), not through its factors. For the binary, ordinal, cbin and frn families uv_max_abs also defaults to 8 and G_max to 20 rather than 50 and 100, so that once a fit separates the data the product \(U G V'\) is bounded on the latent scale instead of running away.

uv_temper_move

Logical, default TRUE. For symmetric Poisson fits with dynamic_uv of the "ar1" kind: every uv_temper_every sweeps (a positive whole number, default 5; a fit with the transition and the uv_nc_move step costs 1.4 times one without them) make a tempered transition (Neal 1996) of one randomly chosen eigen-direction (its weight and coordinate paths, the latent array carried with the predictor), which crosses between the signatures of the weights that the other draws cross only in thousands of sweeps. Recorded in fit$uv_temper_move.

uv_nc_move

Logical, default TRUE. For dynamic_uv of the "ar1" and "snap" kinds: in symmetric fits, draw the persistence rho_uv given the standardised innovations of the paths (the paths then follow the new persistence; a snap reset position, which does not involve it, is held), and in bipartite fits draw the factor by which the paths, the innovation scale sigma_uv and the interaction matrix trade scale at no cost to the predictor (under "snap" with a fixed prior$snap_kappa, the reset positions add their prior ratio). The conditional draws cross these directions slowly (30 to 70 effective draws of 400 for the persistence of a 50-actor symmetric panel). FALSE omits them.

cov_ridge_move

Logical, default TRUE. For directed fits with a row or column covariate (a design slice constant along the columns or the rows) and static coefficients: each sweep also draws, exactly, the amount by which the coefficient and the additive effects of that margin (the levels and, with dynamic_ab, the deviation paths; the intercept takes the constant of the centring) trade against one another without changing any cell's predictor, up to a constant of each period that the latent array absorbs. The conditional draws cross this ridge slowly (the coefficient of a period-varying nodal covariate had 38 to 99 effective draws of 800 on a 170-actor ordinal panel). FALSE omits it.

sparse_position_move

For directed "cbin", "frn" and "ordinal" fits with latent factors (R > 0, not dynamic_uv): each sweep also draws the position of every sender and receiver together with the latent values of its row or column, exactly. Moving \(u_i\) changes the predictor of row \(i\) by a different amount in each column; carrying the latent values along changes no residual, so the conditional of the position is its prior times the indicator that the shifted row is still a latent row the data allow, drawn by an elliptical slice step. Actors the data bound on one side only (no nominations, no nominators, only the lowest category) move across their wide posterior in a few sweeps instead of by random walk. Not applied to "cbin" / "frn" panels with hidden cells. Recorded in fit$sparse_position_move. The coordinate paths of "cbin" and "frn" fits with dynamic_uv of the "ar1" kind (bipartite or directed) move in the same way, each path as a whole, every second sweep unless sparse_position_every says otherwise. An ordinal fit that runs it visits the level translations of actor_move every sweep unless actor_move_every says otherwise.

sparse_position_every

Sweeps between visits of sparse_position_move (default 1: every sweep).

uv_split_move

For directed, symmetric and bipartite fits with latent positions (R > 0, or R_row > 0 and R_col > 0; bipartite fits only with dynamic_uv): draw the split of the scale between the two factors exactly (default TRUE). Multiplying \(U\) by \(c\) and \(V\) by \(1/c\) leaves the product, so the likelihood, unchanged; with the covariance of the rows integrated out the factors have a matrix-t prior, and \(\log c\) is drawn from its density along the orbit by a slice step. The conditional draws of the sweep moved the split by a few percent per sweep against a posterior sd of 0.2 to 0.5 (24 to 54 effective draws of 1,600 in the static directed cells of the acceptance sweep, 4 on a 170-actor ordinal panel); the coordinates of the actors the data say little about, and their products, followed it. For static positions at \(R \ge 2\) the rest of the gauge \(U \to UA\), \(V \to VA^{-T}\) follows under the same prior: one slice step for the scale of each column and one for each shear \(A = I + h e_k e_l'\), which together reach every \(A\) of positive determinant; without them the stretch of \(A\) kept an autocorrelation of 0.9 at lag 20 sweeps and the two-chain check refused a dynamic_rho fit on the split. Static symmetric factors split each column of \(U\) against its eigen-weight. With dynamic_uv = TRUE (directed unipartite fits of every dynamic_uv_kind, and bipartite fits) the same orbit is drawn for the position paths: \(U_t \to cU_t\), \(V_t \to V_t/c\) for all periods together, then for each period alone, each \(\log c\) by a slice step from the AR(1) prior of the paths (with the scale-mixture weights of kind "t" and the resets of kind "snap") and the Jacobian of the map, cut at prior$uv_max_abs. Without it the two-chain check refused fits on the split \(\log(||U_t|| / ||V_t||)\). The paths then draw the rest of their common gauge \(U_t \to U_t A\), \(V_t \to V_t A^{-T}\) for every period together (bipartite paths against \(G \to A^{-1}G\), \(G \to G C^{-T}\)): the scale of each column by a slice step and each shear \(A = I + h e_k e_l'\) as a Gaussian, both from the path prior along the orbit and the Jacobian; symmetric "ar1" and "snap" paths split each column against its weight. The two-chain check monitors the split of symmetric fits too (\(V = UL\), named uv_split as for directed fits). Recorded in fit$uv_split_move (visits, and visits that moved the split). FALSE omits the draw.

uv_rotation_move

For directed unipartite fits with dynamic_uv = TRUE and R >= 2, of every dynamic_uv_kind: draw the orientation of the position paths exactly (default TRUE). \(U_s \to U_s Q\), \(V_s \to V_s Q\) for \(s = t, \dots, N\) with \(Q\) orthogonal (a rotation or a reflection) leaves every \(U_s V_s'\), so the likelihood, unchanged, and changes the AR(1) prior of the paths only through the transition into \(t\); \(Q\) then has a matrix Fisher density (with the scale-mixture weights of kind "t" and the resets of kind "snap"), drawn for each \(t = 2, \dots, N\) one coordinate plane at a time from its two von Mises components, cut at prior$uv_max_abs. Under kind "snap" each plane also tries its mirror image with the resets of that transition summed out, by a Metropolis step, and those resets are then drawn again. The conditional draws cannot reach a reflection, and without the move a kind "snap" chain whose later periods came out reflected against an earlier one explained it by resetting most actors there, so the two-chain check refused rank-2 fits on AR(1) data. Recorded in fit$uv_rotation_move (visits, and visits that moved an orientation). Bipartite fits carry \(U_t G V_t'\) with \(G\) common to the periods and have no such freedom beyond the signs along \(G\). Symmetric "snap" fits at R >= 2 draw the same freedom of \(U_t L U_t'\): for each pair of coordinates, the rotation (weights of one sign) or boost (weights of opposite signs) of the pair in the coordinates scaled by \(|L|^{1/2}\), applied from each period on, by a slice step along its group from the path prior given the resets (the conditional draws turn a period only one actor at a time). FALSE omits the draw.

uv_rho_flip_move

For fits with dynamic_uv = TRUE (unipartite and bipartite, directed and symmetric, every rank and every dynamic_uv_kind): a Metropolis move between \(\rho_{uv}\) and its mirror image, once per sweep (default TRUE). Changing the sign of \(\rho_{uv}\) together with the sign of every position in every second period, \(x_t \to (-1)^{t-1} x_t\) on both sides, leaves each product \(U_t V_t'\) (\(U_t G V_t'\), \(U_t L U_t'\)), so the likelihood, and each transition \(x_t - \rho_{uv} x_{t-1}\) up to its sign, so the AR(1) prior of the paths with its resets and weights; only the prior of \(\rho_{uv}\) tells the two states apart, and the move is accepted with probability \(\min\{1, \pi(-\rho_{uv}) / \pi(\rho_{uv})\}\). Its uniform is the one the draw of \(\rho_{uv}\) in the same sweep used, rescaled, so the move draws no random numbers. The conditional draws of the paths and of \(\rho_{uv}\) cannot cross between the two states: a chain whose \(\rho_{uv}\) passed zero early in the burn-in took alternating period signs and stayed at the negative mirror of the persistence, and the two-chain check refused it on \(\rho_{uv}\). Recorded in fit$uv_rho_flip_move (visits, and visits that moved to the mirror). FALSE omits the move. Since the data see \(|\rho_{uv}|\) only, every stored draw is kept in the gauge \(\rho_{uv} \ge 0\): a draw taken at negative \(\rho_{uv}\) is stored as its mirror (the same likelihood and path prior), so fit$rho_uv, fit$U_draws and fit$V_draws, the forecast states, the two-chain check and trace_plot() all see one gauge; the sampler itself goes on from its state, and fit$start_vals holds that state.

uv_sym_sign_move

For symmetric fits with dynamic_uv = TRUE: an exact draw, every sweep, of the sign of each coordinate path in each period (default TRUE). Changing the sign of coordinate \(r\) of every actor in period \(t\) leaves \(U_t L U_t'\), so the likelihood; the AR(1) prior of the unit-variance paths sees the signs through the products of adjacent periods only (of the drifting transitions under kind "snap", a reset position being symmetric about zero), and the relative signs are drawn from their exact conditional. The conditional draws of the paths cannot change a sign, so without the move two chains could keep different signs in some periods and report different persistences (the two-chain check refused 6 of 24 weakly informed symmetric panels under the default prior, 1 with the move). Recorded in fit$uv_sym_sign_move (visits, and visits that changed a sign). FALSE omits the move.

uv_sym_pair_move

For symmetric fits with dynamic_uv = TRUE of the "ar1" kind and R >= 2 ("snap" fits draw the same group given their resets, see uv_rotation_move): an exact draw, every sweep, of the rest of the gauge of the paths against their weights (default TRUE). \(U_t L U_t'\) is unchanged by \(U_t \to U_t A\) whenever \(A L A' = L\): for two coordinates whose weights have opposite signs \(A\) is a hyperbolic rotation of the coordinates scaled by \(|L_r|^{1/2}\), for two of the same sign a circular one. The angle of each pair is drawn by a slice step from its exact density under the AR(1) prior of the paths, for every period together and from each period on, cut at prior$uv_max_abs. The conditional draws of the paths cannot move along these directions, and without the move a chain at a persistence near 0.9 could sit at a different gauge from the other chain and report a different rho_uv. Recorded in fit$uv_sym_pair_move (visits, and visits that moved a pair). FALSE omits the move.

uv_size_move

For directed and bipartite binary and Poisson fits with dynamic_uv = TRUE: exact draws, every sweep, of the size of the product of the positions in every period together (through \(G\) in bipartite fits, through the paths and sigma_uv in directed ones) and in each period alone (default TRUE). The latent array is integrated out of the binary draws (the dyadic correlation kept through a shared factor) and redrawn after them, and carried with the predictor by the Poisson draws; under kind "t" the weights of the transitions into and out of the period are integrated out and drawn again. The conditional draws move the size of a period's product only as far as the latent array lets them. Recorded in fit$uv_size_move (visits, and visits that moved a size). FALSE omits the draws.

uv_rho_nc_move

For directed and bipartite normal, binary and Poisson fits with dynamic_uv = TRUE, of every dynamic_uv_kind: an exact draw, every sweep, of rho_uv with the stationary variance of the paths and their standardised innovations held, so the paths follow rho_uv and sigma_uv follows the stationary variance (default TRUE). The likelihood of the product enters as for uv_size_move; the unobserved cells of a normal fit are carried. Given the paths rho_uv is pinned far more tightly than its posterior, so its draw alone mixes slowly. Recorded in fit$uv_rho_nc_move (visits, and visits that moved rho_uv). Under "snap", in bipartite fits too, the positions at the resets are held. Symmetric fits draw rho_uv the same way through uv_nc_move. FALSE omits the draw.

ab_shift_move

For directed and bipartite fits without an intercept (intercept = FALSE, the default of "ordinal") with sender and receiver effects (rvar and cvar): draw the shift of the sender effects against the receiver effects exactly (default TRUE). Adding \(c\) to every \(a_i\) and subtracting it from every \(b_j\) leaves every \(a_i + b_j\), so the likelihood, unchanged; only the prior of the effects pins \(c\), and \(c\) is drawn from that normal conditional once per sweep. With dynamic_ab = TRUE the per-actor levels move and the deviations are kept. With an intercept the effects are centred and the draw is not needed. Recorded in fit$ab_shift_move (visits, and visits that moved the effects). FALSE omits the draw.

symmetric_node_tie

For symmetric binary and ordinal fits with a nodal covariate: draw the row and the column coefficient of the covariate as one (default TRUE). The design carries a nodal covariate twice, and the coefficients of its two slices enter the predictor of a symmetric network only through their mean, so the data leave their difference to its prior. The exact symmetric draws of the binary and ordinal families return a difference of the width of that prior, and the draws of the additive effects, of the positions and of the dynamic coefficients that read the predictor carried it as noise: a fit with dynamic_ab and a time-varying nodal covariate let the node coefficient and the effect paths walk off together (the innovation sd of the paths ran to 20 and more against 0.3), and the persistence of dynamic positions was pulled down. Each draw of the coefficients is now followed by replacing the pair by its mean, which keeps the predictor symmetric. Fits without dynamic effects, positions or coefficients, and the normal and Poisson families, are not affected. FALSE restores the earlier draws.

rho_ab_mean

For dynamic_ab=TRUE: Prior mean for additive effects AR(1) parameter (default: 0.8). Controls temporal smoothness of sender/receiver effects.

rho_ab_sd

For dynamic_ab=TRUE: Prior SD for additive effects AR(1) parameter (default: 0.15).

sigma_ab_shape

For dynamic_ab=TRUE: Shape parameter for inverse-gamma prior on additive effects innovation variance (default: 2).

sigma_ab_scale

For dynamic_ab=TRUE: scale parameter of the inverse-gamma prior on the innovation variance of the effect deviations. It is set once before sampling to the prior mean of Sab (that is etaab * Sab0 / (etaab - 3), the mean of the inverse Wishart the covariance is drawn from) times 1 - rho_ab_mean^2, so that a priori the stationary variance of an actor's deviation path matches the variance of the levels and per-period deviations are still pulled toward the actor's level unless the data insist; it is reported as fit$sigma_ab_prior_scale. This is a prior-scale convention. Because it is read off the prior of the additive-effect covariance rather than its current draw, it still follows the scale of the outcome while leaving the sigma_ab and Sab draws as conditionals of one joint density. Set a value to override it.

ab_var_cap

For dynamic_ab=TRUE: optional bound on the stationary variance of an additive-effect path, in the same units as uv_var_cap; the innovation scale is then drawn so that sigma_ab^2 / (1 - rho_ab^2) stays at or below it. Default Inf (no bound). Set it, for example to 4, only when the additive effects themselves are running away; on a near-separable panel a bound here pushes the separation into the interaction matrix instead.

actor_factor_slice

For supported directed binary rank-two AR(1) factor panels with dynamic actor effects and static coefficients, use paired actor/factor elliptical slice updates of the observed likelihood. Default TRUE; FALSE disables this additional transition. Actor centering and factor bounds are preserved.

bipartite_scale_move

For Gaussian, binary, Poisson or ordinal bipartite panels (the last two with actor_move) with moving AR(1) factors and a static interaction matrix: jointly rescale both factor paths, their innovation scale and the interaction matrix (default TRUE). This preserves fitted values and the original posterior target, including all prior bounds. Set FALSE to retain the conditional updates alone.

marginal_move

Run the joint observed-data updates and associated persistence, scale and translation moves for supported binary configurations (default TRUE); see Details.

binary_scale_move

For "binary" fits (every mode, not with dynamic_rho): draw the factor by which the coefficients and the static additive effects are multiplied, exactly and with the latent array integrated out, every binary_scale_every sweeps (default TRUE); FALSE omits it. See Details.

binary_scale_every

For "binary" fits: number of sweeps between draws of that factor (default 5).

level_move_every

For binary unipartite and bipartite fits: number of sweeps between visits of the scale move (default 30).

level_move_tries

For binary unipartite and bipartite fits: proposals per visit of the scale move (default 8). Raising either this or the frequency buys a longer effective sample along the level / spread ridge at a cost per sweep; the visit pays for the factor draw and the latent redraw once, so more proposals per visit are cheaper than more visits.

dev_move

For binary unipartite dynamic_ab fits: walk the second direction of the scale move, the per-period deviations together with sigma_ab (default TRUE). See Details.

dev_move_tries

Proposals per visit along that direction (default 8).

actor_move

For "poisson" and "ordinal" fits (unipartite, directed or symmetric, or bipartite; static or dynamic_ab effects; static coefficients or, for the level translations, dynamic_beta of kind "ar1" or "rw1"): run the translations of the levels with their latent rows and columns, and the further updates listed in Details (default TRUE). For binary fits (unipartite: directed or symmetric, with any additive margin and static coefficients or dynamic_beta of kind "ar1" or "rw1", incomplete panels included; or bipartite with an additive margin or static positions, with static coefficients or dynamic_beta of kind "ar1" or "rw1"): run the collapsed per-actor update (default TRUE). For "cbin" and "frn" fits (unipartite or bipartite, static or dynamic_ab levels, static coefficients or dynamic_beta of kind "ar1" or "rw1" on the unit period grid, with or without dynamic_beta_per_actor): run the receiver-level translation, with an intercept the level update, and for directed fits with dcor = TRUE the reciprocity update; the sender translation of a dynamic_ab fit runs under the same switch (default TRUE). With dynamic_uv, Poisson and binary fits also redraw the position paths (actor_move_paths). See Details.

chain_extensions

Number of times the chains are continued while the drift check or the between-chain check flags them (a drifting chain, an R-hat above its threshold, or a series with too few effective draws to compare the chains; default 3). Chains that still drift or disagree after the last extension are refused with an error of class lame_chain_unsettled; chains still too short to compare are returned with a warning of class lame_chain_not_compared; 0 decides on the first block. An extension is a block of nscan sweeps, longer when series are short of effective draws (see the convergence policy).

actor_move_every

Number of sweeps between visits of the collapsed per-actor update (default 10), of the translations of the Poisson (default 2) and ordinal (default 10) families or of the receiver-level translation and the level, period and room updates of "cbin" and "frn" fits, and of the sender translation of their dynamic_ab fits (default 1; their reciprocity update runs on every tenth visit). The position paths of a dynamic_uv_kind = "snap" fit are visited every sweep (a binary fit by default; the other families always, Poisson with its translations).

actor_move_rho

For directed fits with dcor = TRUE, also update the dyadic correlation with the latent responses integrated out at each visit of the collapsed per-actor update (default TRUE); for "cbin" and "frn" fits it switches the reciprocity update.

actor_move_period

For "cbin" and "frn" fits with a dynamic_beta intercept: also translate the intercept of the periods that the rows with room do not tie together, period by period (default TRUE; FALSE keeps the common translation of the level update only). See Details.

actor_move_room

For "cbin" and "frn" fits with a dynamic_beta intercept: also move the intercept of each period that has rows with room, with the non-nominations of those rows integrated out (default TRUE). See Details.

beta_hyper_nc

For dynamic_beta fits: run the interweaving step that moves the hyperparameters of the coefficient paths with the path (default TRUE); FALSE omits it and keeps the draws at every sweep. See the dynamic_beta argument.

poisson_period_move

For "poisson" fits with dynamic_beta: translate every period, and the whole path, of each dynamic coefficient with its latent slice at every sweep (default TRUE); FALSE omits them. See Details.

poisson_static_move

For "poisson" fits with dynamic_beta and static coefficients: translate each static coefficient with the whole latent array every actor_move_every sweeps (default TRUE).

ordinal_scale_move

For "ordinal" fits (unipartite and bipartite, static or dynamic coefficients and effects): draw, at every sweep, the scale of the whole state (the coefficients, the static additive effects and the latent array together, with the free cutpoints of ordinal_cutpoints = "explicit") and, with the default data-induced cutpoints, the shift and the scale of the latent array of each period alone, each exactly along a transformation that keeps every rank (default TRUE); FALSE omits them. See Details.

actor_hyper_nc

For dynamic_beta_per_actor fits: run the interweaving step that moves the innovation variance and the persistence of the actor-specific paths with the paths (default TRUE); FALSE omits it and keeps the draws at every sweep.

actor_move_paths

For Poisson and binary fits with moving positions (dynamic_uv = TRUE), and for every family under kind "snap": redraw the whole position path of each actor at each visit (default TRUE), under kind "snap" with the resets summed out and then drawn again; FALSE omits it and leaves the other updates of actor_move as they are. See Details.

ab_hyper_move

For dynamic_ab fits with an additive margin (every family and mode): draw the level variances (their covariance for directed unipartite fits), the innovation scale and the persistence of the additive effects given their totals with the levels integrated out (default TRUE). See Details.

ab_hyper_move_tries

Proposals per sweep of that update (default 8).

ab_period_move

For "poisson" fits with dynamic_ab: move each actor-period effect together with the latent values of its row (column), in pairs when the effects of a period sum to zero, exactly and at every sweep (default TRUE). See Details.

uv_g_scale_move

For bipartite fits with static positions: draw the scale split between the positions and the interaction matrix exactly (default TRUE). See Details.

als_start

For directed unipartite dynamic_uv fits of the "ar1" or "t" kind (normal, Poisson or binary outcome): start the chain from a dynamic AR(1) ALS fit of the same model (default TRUE; see Details). FALSE keeps the cold start.

snap_kappa

For dynamic_uv_kind = "snap": the sd of the position a reset lands on. Unset (the default), a reset is a fresh draw from the stationary distribution of the position paths, \(\kappa^2 = \sigma_{uv}^2 / (1 - \rho_{uv}^2)\), recomputed every sweep, and the reset positions enter the rho_uv and sigma_uv draws as stationary draws. A positive number fixes the scale. A fixed scale well above the positions' spread makes a reset implausible for any ordinary jump; choose this scale in the units of the latent coordinates (the unit-variance paths of a symmetric fit, whose linked scale is 1).

rho_beta_mean

For dynamic_beta: Prior mean for the per-block AR(1) parameter on time-varying regression coefficients (default: 0.8). Closer to 1 = smoother evolution.

rho_beta_sd

For dynamic_beta: Prior SD for the per-block AR(1) parameter (default: 0.15).

rho_beta_lower

For dynamic_beta: Lower truncation bound on the AR(1) parameter (default: 0). Pass a negative value to allow negative autoregression.

rho_beta_upper

For dynamic_beta: Upper truncation bound (default: 0.999). Closer to 1 admits near-unit-root behaviour.

sigma_beta_shape

For dynamic_beta: shape parameter of the inverse-Gamma prior on the per-block innovation variance (default: 2). The conditional combines this proper prior with the coefficient path's quadratic form and effective dimension under its selected temporal law. With few transitions informing a coefficient block the posterior of the innovation variance stays near this prior.

sigma_beta_scale

For dynamic_beta: scale parameter of the inverse-Gamma prior on the per-block innovation variance. It is set once before sampling from the response scale: the innovation covariance of the coefficient path is sigma_beta^2 Lambda with Lambda the g-prior scale matrix, so sigma_beta is the per-period innovation sd of a covariate's contribution to the linear predictor in the units of the response. The default prior mean innovation variance is 0.04 times the residual variance (the variance of the two-way centred outcome for the normal and poisson families, 1 for the probit and rank families, whose latent scale is fixed). It is reported as fit$sigma_beta_prior_scale. Set a value to override it.

sigma_beta_init

For dynamic_beta: Initial value of the per-block innovation standard deviation (default: 0.25; 0.25 * sd(Y) for the normal family). Affects mixing, not the stationary distribution.

beta0_mean

For dynamic_beta: Mean of the Gaussian prior on the first observed coefficient state under RW1 (default: 0). An AR(1) path starts from its stationary law around its long-run mean, whose prior is that of a static coefficient (see dynamic_beta).

beta0_var

For dynamic_beta: Variance of the Gaussian prior on the first observed coefficient state under RW1 (default: 10; 10 * var(Y) for the normal family, in the unit of the response). This prior is independent of the sampled evolution parameters. RW2 uses its proper difference-precision prior and Matern 3/2 its covariance kernel over all observed periods instead.

Common usage: prior = list(Sab0 = diag(c(1, 1)), eta0 = 10) for stronger shrinkage, or prior = list(rho_uv_mean = 0.95) for higher temporal persistence, or prior = list(rho_beta_mean = 0.95, sigma_beta_scale = 0.01) for very smooth time-varying coefficients with tight innovations.

g

optional scalar or vector for g-prior on regression coefficients. Default is n^2, where n is the number of actors (nA for a bipartite fit). The prior of the normal family scales with the response, for every unit of Y. The static coefficients of a unipartite fit have the panel prior with precision sum_t(crossprod(X_t)) / (T g), whatever the residual variance, and take g = n^2 * var(Y) (n^2 where the link fixes the scale); when other coefficients have paths (dynamic_beta, or the intercept path that dynamic_ab adds), the static ones keep the marginal of that same prior, so the prior of a static slope does not depend on whether another coefficient moves. The coefficients of a bipartite fit have the prior N(0, g s2), whose s2 already carries the unit, and take n^2 divided, for a slope, by the mean square of its covariate, with or without paths. In both modes the unit of a covariate only rescales its coefficient. The g-prior controls the variance of regression coefficients: larger values allow for larger coefficient values. Can be a vector of length p for parameter-specific control.

seed

random seed for the MCMC sampler (default 6886). The sampler is seeded internally with this value, so results are reproducible by default and an external set.seed() call has no effect on the chain – pass a different seed here to vary the draws (e.g. when running multiple chains). The caller's .Random.seed is restored on exit, so fitting never perturbs your RNG stream. Changing nscan or burn changes the whole chain, not only its length, because the sweep permutations are drawn up front; to lengthen a finished chain use lame_resume.

nscan

number of iterations of the Markov chain (beyond burn-in)

burn

burn in for the Markov chain

odens

output density for the Markov chain

plot

logical: plot results while running?

verbose

logical: print progress while running? Default FALSE.

gof

logical: calculate goodness of fit statistics?

start_vals

list of parameter starting values for the MCMC chain. Tempered fits accept their own fit$start_vals replica matrix as a warm start; use lame_resume for exact continuation. dynamic_uv fits of the "ar1" kind start from a dynamic ALS fit by default when this is NULL (see Details). Use als_start_vals to start MCMC from an ALS fit, or the start_vals element of a previous fit to continue from its final state. Recognised slots are Z, beta, a, b, U, V, rho, s2, Sab and, for dynamic fits, the scalars rho_uv, sigma_uv, rho_ab and sigma_ab; bipartite fits also take G, use a slot only when its shape matches the panel and warn about the ones they skip. The rho_uv and rho_ab values that als_start_vals emits are the penalty settings of the ALS fit rather than estimates (for an empirical-Bayes fit, the default for normal, binary and Poisson panels, they are estimates); they only seed the chain.

periodic_save

logical: indicating whether to periodically save MCMC results

out_file

character vector indicating name and path in which file should be stored if periodic_save is selected. For example, on an Apple OS out_file="~/Desktop/ameFit.rda".

save_interval

quantile interval indicating when to save during the post-burn-in period.

model.name

optional string for model selection output

save_log_lik

one of FALSE (default), TRUE, or "chunked". When TRUE, stores the per-iteration pointwise log-likelihood matrix on fit$log_lik (an [n_stored, n_obs] double matrix). When "chunked", streams the log-lik values to per-column-chunk binary files under log_lik_path so the in-memory cost during MCMC is just one chunk's width; the chunks are recovered later via read_log_lik(fit). Required for loo::loo(fit) and loo::waic(fit).

posterior_opts

optional list of posterior draw-storage options, either a plain list() or one built with posterior_options (which spells the position option save_UV). Recognised names (unknown names trigger a warning): save_UV, save_UV_draws, save_ab, thin_UV, thin_ab. save_UV = TRUE and save_UV_draws = TRUE are aliases on this path. With dynamic_uv = TRUE they store the per-iteration dynamic latent-position cubes at every stored (odens) iteration on fit$U_draws / fit$V_draws, each an [actor, dim, period, draw] array. On a static fit with a positive multiplicative rank they store the per-iteration latent-position matrices on fit$U_samples / fit$V_samples ([actor, dim, draw] arrays, as ame does). Bipartite fits with positive latent ranks additionally store the interaction-matrix draws on fit$G_samples ([R_row, R_col, draw]). save_ab = TRUE stores identified additive-effect draws in a_samples / b_samples (actor by draw) for static effects, or a_draws / b_draws (actor by period by draw) for dynamic effects, with actor-level draws in a_level_samples / b_level_samples. thin_ab thins the retained coefficient draws further; ab_draw_index records their matching row indices. Compact joint terminal states are always retained on fit$forecast_state for posterior forecasts, even when full actor and position trajectories are not requested. thin_UV remains accepted for compatibility but is not applied here (odens already thins the stored chain). Requesting latent draw storage with a zero multiplicative rank warns and stores nothing. Default NULL.

log_lik_path

directory to write log-lik chunks to when save_log_lik = "chunked". Default NULL creates a session-scoped subdirectory under tempdir(). With several chains, chain k writes to its own directory, <log_lik_path>_chain<k>, and read_log_lik(fit) returns the chains stacked in the order of the pooled draws. lame_resume() writes the block it adds to <log_lik_path>_resume<k>, so the chunks of the fit it continues stay readable.

log_lik_chunk_size

column-width of each on-disk chunk when save_log_lik = "chunked". Larger chunks mean fewer files (and one readBin per chunk on read) but more memory during MCMC. Default 10000L.

keep_snap_draws

controls storage of post-burn-in MCMC snap-shift indicators when dynamic_uv = TRUE and dynamic_uv_kind = "snap". "none" keeps only the posterior mean snap probabilities. "summary" stores cell-level count, mean, and variance summaries. "draws" stores retained binary indicator arrays as fit$snap_draws and, for directed and bipartite fits (the column actors of a bipartite fit), fit$snap_draws_v, with dimensions draw x actor x time and first period set to NA.

freeze_call

logical: if TRUE, store a snapshot of the evaluated Y, Xdyad, Xrow, Xcol on fit$data_snapshot so that a later update(fit, ...) refits against the same data even if the caller has mutated those objects in their workspace. Memory cost equals the size of the data; default FALSE.

dynamic_beta_pool

one of "none" (default), "rho", "sigma", or "both". When two or more coefficient blocks are dynamic, non-"none" values update shared hyperparameters across blocks for the selected persistence and / or innovation-scale component. Persistence pooling uses a Gaussian hierarchy on the logit of (rho - rho_beta_lower) / (rho_beta_upper - rho_beta_lower), with a normal mean prior and inverse-Gamma variance prior. Its current mean and scale are retained in checkpoint state. With a single dynamic block the value is recorded but there is no other block to pool against. On method = "als" the empirical-Bayes estimator honours it: "sigma" shares the innovation scales across the dynamic blocks, "rho" pools the first-order persistences through the same logit-normal hierarchy as the sampler (a random-walk block has none to pool), "both" does both; the penalised routes name it in the warning about ignored arguments.

dynamic_beta_per_actor

optional, one of NULL (default), "row", or "col". When non-NULL, fits actor-specific time-varying deviations for one dyadic covariate on the selected margin. The default per_actor_identifiability = "center" keeps the population coefficient in coef(fit) and enforces a per-period sum-to-zero constraint on the actor deviations. Their innovation variance defaults to an inverse-Gamma(2, 1) prior (scale var(Y) for the normal family: the unit of the response), configurable through prior$sigma_actor_shape and prior$sigma_actor_scale. The transformed persistence \((1 + \rho)/2\) defaults to a Beta(2, 2) prior, with shapes prior$rho_actor_shape1 and prior$rho_actor_shape2, restricted to \(-0.99 < \rho < 0.99\), with a stationary initial state. Priors act on the centered subspace with one fewer dimension than the actor count. All four hyperparameters must be finite and positive. Choose the innovation scale for the outcome and covariate units. Stored fits record these choices in per_actor_prior. Draws are stored in fit$THETA_ACTOR when retained; summary mode stores fit$theta_actor_mean and fit$theta_actor_sd. The innovation variance and the persistence are drawn from their exact conditionals at every sweep from the first one, and an interweaving step moves them together with the paths (prior$actor_hyper_nc). Where each actor's data say little about its path, which is the usual case, the draws at every sweep leave them with 220 to 900 effective draws in 2,000, and the step multiplies that by 1.1 to 2.4.

per_actor_covariate_idx

positive integer; index into the dyadic covariate cube to slope on for the per-actor extension. Default 1L.

per_actor_identifiability

one of "center" (default) or "exact_center". "center" preserves the population coefficient and constrains the per-actor deviations to sum to zero per period via pairwise contrast FFBS. "exact_center" draws each actor's path from its own conditional AR(1) posterior and conditions on all period-wise sum-to-zero constraints using the complete temporal covariance. Dyadic reciprocity couples actors; that case uses a joint Gaussian draw on the constrained subspace, at a higher cost per sweep.
